recap_title: 🎯 Quick & Visual Recap: Laravel PHP Backend (Web)
recap_subtitle: Welcome, hero! This is a quick review supported by programming examples and illustrations for each session you learned in the course to help you remember the concepts with ease and fun and prepare for the super exam! 🚀🌟

points.title: Configure the local environment and install Laravel
points.desc: Install a XAMPP server to provide a local server with a MySQL database, and use the Composer package manager to download and install the Laravel framework.

points.title: Running your first Laravel project
points.desc: Create a new Laravel project and run the internal development server by calling simple commands.
points.code:
composer create-project laravel/laravel my-web-app
cd my-web-app
php artisan serve
points.example: Open a web browser and go to the link http://127.0.0.1:8000 to see the Laravel welcome interface.

points.title: Understanding the MVC architecture for websites
points.desc: An architecture that separates data storage logic (Model), user interfaces (View), and process coordinator (Controller).

points.title: Writing basic routes
points.desc: Directing the browser to display a specific interface or execute a specific throwing command when a specific URL is requested.
points.example: Direct the user to view the welcome page by simply typing the link /welcome.

points.title: Passing variables via links (Route Parameters)
points.desc: Receiving variable values ​​directly from the URL (such as the cookie code number) and processing them within the path.

points.title: Named paths and path groups
points.desc: Naming paths to facilitate their recall in interfaces, and grouping similar paths under a unified prefix such as the control panel.
points.example: Group store administration routes with a unified prefix: Route::prefix('admin').

points.title: Blade display template engine
points.desc: A smart and attractive engine in Laravel that allows writing complex HTML codes combined with PHP code very smoothly and without clutter.

points.title: Designing the unified structure of the site (Master Layout)
points.desc: Design a unified main web template (containing the header and footer) and inherit it for all sub-pages of the site to prevent duplication of codes.
points.code:
@yield('main_content') @extends('layouts.master') @section('main_content')

This is the content of the home page!

@endsection
points.example: Building a template for the basic structure of the site and inheriting it to the store and contact us pages.

points.title: Loops and Conditions in Blade
points.desc: Use simple directives like foreach and if to dynamically display products and cakes based on data.

points.title: View interactive product listings
points.desc: Display arrays of items and prices in elegant tables and display a default message if the cart is empty.
points.example: View the list of birthday cakes with updated prices in the storefront.

points.title: Controllers
points.desc: Dedicated programming classes to separate the script's decision-making logic from the main path file to organize the application.

points.title: Connecting paths to controllers
points.desc: Automatically directs browser requests to a specific function within the controller to process data and display the appropriate page.
points.example: Call the function to display cake products from the database immediately after requesting the main store page.

points.title: Database Migrants
points.desc: An intelligent database tracking and versioning system in Laravel that allows you to create and modify tables programmatically without the need to write SQL.

points.title: Design product tables and cakes
points.desc: Build text and numeric fields and timestamps for site tables and implement instant synchronization with MySQL server.
points.example: Build a table of bakery cakes and customize the Name, Description, Price, and Availability fields.

points.title: Database Seeding
points.desc: A smart tool for feeding and filling tables with fictitious and virtual data useful for site scanning and testing purposes.

points.title: Advanced mock data generation
points.desc: Use the popular Faker library to generate hundreds of random, realistic names, addresses, and prices at a glance.
points.example: Generate 50 random cookies at varying prices to test browsing efficiency and site speed.

points.title: Smart ORM (Eloquent)
points.desc: Laravel's entity handling engine. Each table in the database is linked to a model to facilitate data queries.

points.title: Fast query and search script
points.desc: Read or filter all records and search for a specific cookie using powerful and shortcut functions and without complex SQL.
points.example: Display only chocolate cakes in the section filter interface.

points.title: Processing input forms (HTML Forms)
points.desc: Receiving data and inputs written by website visitors (such as adding a new cake to the store) and directing them to the controller.

points.title: Site protected by @csrf
points.desc: A built-in and enforceable security mechanism in Laravel to protect the site from cross-site pharming attacks and secure form reception.
points.example: Attach the automatic security code @csrf to the registration form to purchase the cake.

points.title: Validation of inputs
points.desc: Prevent any false or empty data from being saved by checking the quality of the input and ensuring that it conforms to the programming laws.

points.title: Display warning and error messages
points.desc: Displaying clear and interactive Arabic alert messages to the user when they forget to fill out one of the required fields.
points.example: Alert the user that the 'Price' field must contain numbers only.

points.title: Basic operations (Create & Read)
points.desc: Save new approved data in MySQL tables, read it and display it in a dynamic and fast way in the interfaces.

points.title: Add cake products to the database
points.desc: Add and store new cakes with name and price, save them in the store, and successfully redirect the admin to the control panel page.
points.example: Submit your new cake template and save it immediately to appear in your store's product list.

points.title: Edit & Delete (Update & Delete)
points.desc: Update the prices and information of cakes or remove them and delete them completely from the database when the available quantity in the store runs out.

points.title: Delete an item from the store
points.desc: Search for the chosen item by sub-identifier, delete it with a glance, and display a notification stating the success of the operation to the user.
points.example: Press the trash button to delete a damaged cake from the store control panel.

points.title: Site security and login
points.desc: Building a website security system and ensuring the protection of buyers and moderators' accounts using encryption technologies built into Laravel.

points.title: Verify and confirm the buyer's account
points.desc: Automatic verification of mail and encrypted password and opening a secure browsing session for the user.
points.example: Prevent browsing the administrative control panel until you successfully type the correct password.

points.title: Upload and store photos and files
points.desc: Providing the administrator with the opportunity to upload pictures of delicious cakes, store the files safely on the application servers, and link the image path to the database.

points.title: Save and display product images
points.desc: Confirm receipt of the image file, save it to the public storage folder, and view the cake art in the store.
points.example: Download and view the newly uploaded high-quality birthday cake image in the store.

sessions.session_title: Session 16: Mega Project - Dynamic Cake Shop Website

points.title: The culmination of a challenging project
points.desc: Bringing together all the techniques we've learned to build a full-fledged magic cake shop, featuring a customer screen and a comprehensive admin screen.

points.title: Browse and book dream cakes
points.desc: A screen that allows visitors to browse available cakes, reserve cakes, and write their feedback with the interactive shopping cart.
points.example: An integrated, locally published cake store application that connects all interfaces to one live and active database!
